title: Recruiting Screen - Danielle Ross
summary: 30-minute initial recruiting screen for SWE IC-2/3 role. Candidate has 4 years backend infra experience at Streamline AI, strong Python and distributed systems exposure; open to remote-first role, prefers Seattle timezone. Agreed next step: schedule technical interview + coding challenge; recruiter to confirm comp band and availability.
next_steps: Claire Park: send tech screen calendar invite (aim for 2025-09-18 to 2025-09-22)
Amit Verma: prepare high-level system-design focus areas for technical interview
Danielle Ross: complete short take-home coding challenge within 72 hours if invited
action_items: Claire Park: confirm target comp band and share by 2025-09-16
Tom Alvarez: upload Danielle's resume to ATS and tag Eng Manager
Danielle Ross: provide two time windows for next week for technical interview
transcript: [00:00] Claire Park: Hey Danielle, thanks for making time today, how are you?
[00:06] Danielle Ross: I'm good thanks, Claire, excited to chat about the role at Redwood. Hope that's okay — I like what I saw in the job posting.
[00:12] Tom Alvarez: (background) quick intro—I'm Tom from recruiting, helping coordinate — won't take much of your time.
[00:18] Claire Park: Quick agenda: 1) high level background, 2) what you're looking for, 3) logistics (comp, notice, work auth), 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Danielle Ross: Yep that sounds great.
[00:32] Claire Park: Can you walk us through your last two roles — titles, main responsibilities?

[00:40] Danielle Ross: Sure. I'm currently a Software Engineer II at Streamline AI — been there about 2.5 years. Focused on backend infra for model orchestration — things like job scheduling, retries, KV cache-ish systems, and integrating different model runtimes. Before that I was at BrightMetrics as a backend dev, mostly Go services and some infra automation. Sorry, I might say KV cache as K-V cash sometimes, lol, transcripts love that word.
[01:12] Amit Verma: (interject) nice, can you give an example of a system you owned end-to-end?

[01:17] Danielle Ross: Yeah—last quarter I led a project building a live job scheduler for low-latency model retraining. We had to balance throughput and latency, the scheduler did prioritization, prefetching model weights to avoid cold starts, and handled node drain resiliency. I wrote the scheduler logic, worked on metrics/alerts, and collaborated with infra to tune GC and memory for the model runners.
[01:48] Claire Park: Sounds relevant. Which languages and infra are you most comfortable with?

[01:52] Danielle Ross: Primarily Python and Go. We run a mix — orchestration layers are Python, performance-critical pieces in Go. Kubernetes for orchestration, some custom RPC, Redis and S3 for artifacts. Familiar with Docker, CI/CD, and basic perf tuning.
[02:10] Amit Verma: Do you have hands-on experience with GPU infra or quantization pipelines?

[02:14] Danielle Ross: I haven't done kernel-level optimizations, but I worked closely with ML infra teams to provision GPU pools, set up autoscaling, and run cost/perf benchmarks. I've read about quantization but haven't implemented it in prod.

[02:28] Claire Park: That's totally fine for this role. We're hiring for someone to help build the serving runtime and tooling, so infra experience and product sense matter as much as low-level kernels.
[02:37] Danielle Ross: Good to know. My interest is in latency-sensitive infra, so that aligns.
[02:41] Tom Alvarez: Quick logistics — are you currently open to relocating or prefer remote?
[02:45] Danielle Ross: I'm remote-first. I'm in Seattle and would prefer remote or hybrid; open to occasional travel for offsites.
[02:53] Claire Park: Work authorization?
[02:55] Danielle Ross: US citizen.
[02:57] Amit Verma: What about notice period and current comp? We ask for ranges.
[03:02] Danielle Ross: I have a 2-week notice. Current base is $150k, total comp roughly $175k with bonus and RSUs. Looking for something in the 170-210k range depending on level and equity.
[03:18] Claire Park: Great, that's helpful. For level calibration, can you tell me about a recent bug or incident you troubleshot?

[03:25] Danielle Ross: Sure — we had intermittent OOMs in one of our model runners after a GC change. I triaged memory profiles, isolated a leak caused by cached preprocessed assets not being freed, added reference counting and eviction policy, and collaborated with infra to bump memory and schedule a canary. That reduced OOMs by 90% in two weeks.
[03:53] Amit Verma: Nice. How comfortable are you with coding interviews? Whiteboard or take-home?

[03:58] Danielle Ross: I'm comfortable with both; prefer a short take-home for system-level problems but can do a live coding too. My strongest are algorithms around graphs and distributed systems patterns.

[04:08] Claire Park: For our loop we typically do a 60-minute coding phone screen with an engineer (live), then a system design 60–90 min with an Eng Manager. We can be flexible and offer a take-home if preferred. Any constraints?
[04:20] Danielle Ross: No constraints, 9am-2pm PT generally works best for me during the week.
[04:27] Tom Alvarez: Got it. Any non-negotiables or dealbreakers we should know about?
[04:30] Danielle Ross: Not really. I want meaningful ownership and a team that cares about infra quality. Compensation is flexible.
[04:36] Claire Park: Cool. A couple more quick things: do you have experience mentoring or reviewing code?
[04:41] Danielle Ross: Yes, I've mentored two junior engineers and run code reviews regularly. I try to focus on clarity and testability.
[04:48] Amit Verma: Do you have any questions for us about the role or the team?
[04:52] Danielle Ross: Yeah—what's the primary focus in the first 6 months for this role?

[04:57] Claire Park: Good question. For IC-2 we'd expect to own a service or two, improve latency and cost profiles, and contribute to rollout/monitoring infra. For IC-3 more cross-team ownership and design. Amit, can you add detail?

[05:10] Amit Verma: Sure—first 6 months involves onboarding into our runtime, shipping an optimization (batching/cache) and owning incident response for a route. Lots of collaboration with research and infra teams.
[05:24] Danielle Ross: That sounds like what I want to be doing.
[05:27] Claire Park: Anything else on benefits or comp structure you want clarified?
[05:31] Danielle Ross: Are RSUs typical for mid-level?
[05:34] Amit Verma: Yes, we provide equity grants at hire; range depends on level. We'll share approximate bands following this call.
[05:41] Claire Park: Last logistics: are there any background or security checks you anticipate being an issue?
[05:45] Danielle Ross: No, no problems.

[05:47] Claire Park: Great. I'll recap next steps—Claire to send calendar invite for tech phone screen, Amit to outline focus areas, Danielle to confirm availability and optionally do a take-home. Any blockers?
[05:58] Danielle Ross: None from me.
[06:00] Tom Alvarez: (background) I'll update ATS and tag you all.
[06:04] Claire Park: Awesome — thanks Danielle, we'll follow up via email with times and a short prep note. Have a great afternoon.
[06:12] Danielle Ross: Thanks, you too! Bye.
[34:59] (call end)
